editorial:
Imagine being dropped right into the middle of a sweaty, loud crowd at the Hammerstein Ballroom in New York City. You get to see Korn at the top of their game during the Untouchables tour, bringing all that raw energy and heavy sound straight to your living room. The vibe is pure chaos in the best way possible, with Jonathan Davis jumping around the stage and the band cranking out hits from their biggest albums. It feels less like a polished movie and more like you are actually standing in the front row getting pushed around by other fans.

What really makes this stand out is the double DVD setup. You get the main show first, but then you can watch it again from different camera angles, which is a cool touch for any music lover. The pacing is fast and loud, though some of the behind-the-scenes clips feel a bit short. If you love nu-metal or just want to see a band giving it their all, you need to see this. Since it is an older release, your best bet is hunting down the physical DVD for your collection or checking if it is available to rent on Apple TV for a nostalgic trip.
endingExplained: The show wraps up with the band playing their most famous hits to a wild crowd. You get to see the final energy burst as the musicians leave the stage, leaving the fans screaming for more. It ends with a glimpse of their cover of Metallica's One, showing how much they respect the legends. There is no big plot twist here since it is a concert, but it closes by showing the bond between the band and their fans.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves early 2000s rock and heavy music.
